evidence_items.finding: bookings have been flat at approximately 28 per year for 14 months despite tripling advertising spend from $800 to $2,400/month
evidence_items.rationale: Flat bookings despite tripling advertising spend is a critical adverse conversion signal. market_position; is_critical=true.

evidence_items.finding: enquiries from the website have grown 40% over six months but bookings have not grown — conversion rate is therefore declining
evidence_items.rationale: Growing enquiries with flat bookings implies a declining conversion rate that has not been tracked or investigated. market_position; is_critical=true.

evidence_items.finding: enquiry responses are sent informally by email when the owner is available, with no documented follow-up process
evidence_items.rationale: Informal reactive enquiry response without documented follow-up is a critical adverse conversion process signal. process_maturity; is_critical=true.

evidence_items.finding: the owner has never calculated the enquiry-to-booking conversion rate
evidence_items.rationale: Absence of conversion rate tracking while planning to increase spend is an adverse evidence signal. process_maturity.

evidence_items.finding: wedding photography; $2,400/month ad spend; website traffic doubled; enquiries up 40%; bookings flat at 28/year for 14 months; no conversion tracking; informal email response
Surface signal (not root cause): website traffic doubling and enquiries growing 40% suggests the advertising is working and the problem is targeting
evidence_items.rationale: Rising traffic and enquiries is a misleading channel-performance signal — if enquiries are growing but bookings are flat, the issue is in the conversion step after enquiry, not the advertising reach.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): the most obvious explanation for rising enquiries with flat bookings is that the ads are reaching the wrong type of client
evidence_items.rationale: Audience mismatch is a misleading default explanation when conversion process data is absent — an informal response process could equally explain the conversion failure.

validation_notes: SIM-13-007 is SUPPORTED via demand_generation_failure. Flat bookings with rising enquiries and absent conversion tracking maps to demand generation failure. No must_identify vocabulary.
